title: The Week I Finally Saw a Therapist
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] For almost two years, I told myself therapy was only for people with serious problems, not for someone like me.
Narrator: [honest] Meanwhile, I was barely sleeping, snapping at coworkers, and feeling numb during moments that should have made me happy.
Narrator: [reflective] My sister noticed before I did. She said I sounded exhausted in every phone call, even when I insisted I was fine.
Narrator: [honest] I brushed off her concern several times, although deep down, I knew something in me had quietly stopped working properly.
Narrator: [determined] Finally, after a difficult week at work, I searched online and booked an appointment with a therapist named Rian.
Narrator: [nervous] Walking into his office the first time, my hands were shaking, and I almost turned around at the door.
Narrator: [honest] He asked simple questions first, like how I was sleeping, and whether I still enjoyed things I used to love.
Narrator: [reflective] I answered honestly, and saying the words out loud felt strange, since I had never described my feelings so directly before.
Narrator: [thoughtful] He explained that burnout often disguises itself as laziness or bad mood, when really the mind is overwhelmed.
Narrator: [relieved] Hearing that made me cry a little, although I quickly apologized, embarrassed by my own reaction in front of a stranger.
Narrator: [warmly] He told me crying in that room was normal, and probably overdue after two years of pretending.
Narrator: [thoughtful] We talked about setting boundaries at work, since I had been answering emails late at night without resting.
Narrator: [determined] So I started turning off notifications after seven, even though my manager questioned it that first week.
Narrator: [hopeful] Slowly, my sleep improved, and I noticed myself laughing genuinely again, something I had almost forgotten how to do.
Narrator: [grateful] My sister was right all along, although I needed to reach my own breaking point before I could truly hear her.
Narrator: [warmly] Now I see Rian every two weeks, not because something is broken, but because maintenance matters for the mind too.
Narrator: [reflective] I used to believe asking for help meant weakness, but I understand now it required real courage.
Narrator: [peacefully] If someone told me a year ago that therapy would change my life this much, I would not have believed them.

options: That it was only for people with serious problems, not him
quiz.explanation: He told himself therapy was only for people with serious problems, not for someone like him.
